subfield: enumerative geometry of space curves; ruled surfaces
well_posed_note: 'Axes des plans osculateurs' is ambiguous. It may mean the binormals (normals to the osculating planes at the curve points) or the polar lines (normals to the osculating planes through the centres of curvature). Degrees (b) and (c) also require genericity of $C$ with respect to the absolute conic. Only (a) is projectively meaningful.

elementary_check.plan: For m=n=2 (a quartic of genus 1), one could count numerically how many tangent lines, principal normals or binormals meet a random line. That count is the degree of each ruled surface; one would compare (a) with 8. Doing this robustly requires solving polynomial systems with spurious solutions at infinity, which is too fragile for a quick script.

belief.note: Part (a), the tangent developable having degree $mn(m+n-2)$, is classical (Salmon, Cayley). Degrees of the principal-normal and binormal surfaces were computed in the later 19th-century literature on space curves, but I cannot quote exact formulas or references with confidence.
